questions.question_text: Which organelle is known as the 'powerhouse' of the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are responsible for generating most of the cell's supply of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), the source of chemical energy.

questions.question_text: What is the process by which plants convert sunlight into energy?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is the process used by plants to convert light energy into chemical energy.

questions.question_text: What is the primary function of red blood cells?
questions.explanation: Red blood cells contain hemoglobin which binds to oxygen for transport.

questions.question_text: Which molecule carries genetic information in most organisms?
questions.explanation: DNA contains the hereditary instructions for all living organisms.

questions.question_text: What is the process of cell division resulting in two identical daughter cells?
questions.explanation: Mitosis is the somatic cell division that creates identical clones.

questions.question_text: Which part of the cell is known as the 'powerhouse'?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are responsible for generating most of the cell's supply of adenosine triphosphate (ATP).

questions.question_text: What is the name of the process plants use to turn sunlight into energy?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is the process used by plants to convert light energy into chemical energy.

questions.question_text: What is the main role of red blood cells?
questions.explanation: Red blood cells contain hemoglobin, which binds to oxygen and carries it throughout the body.

questions.question_text: Which molecule stores genetic information in most living things?
questions.explanation: Deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) is the primary carrier of genetic instructions.

questions.question_text: What is the specific type of cell division that creates two identical daughter cells?
questions.explanation: Mitosis is the process of nuclear division in eukaryotic cells that occurs when a parent cell divides to produce two identical daughter cells.
